existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: Provenance has several local R4→R6 breaking changes: `reason` was removed/split, the required `entity.role` code set changed, and `agent.onBehalfOf` removed Device/RelatedPerson targets. The largest R6→R4 risks are optional `recorded`, new context elements, and new agent target types. Confidence is high for structure-level changes; terminology mapping details need official expansions and change notes.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is less about a single cardinality tightening and more about **semantic remodeling**: reason/authorization/why, functional vs structural agent roles, stricter delegation rules, and a changed entity role vocabulary. R4→R6 pipelines need explicit transforms for removed fields and invalid codes; R6→R4 pipelines need extensions or rejection policies for new fields and missing `recorded`.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present and the most important differences are computable in the snapshots/differentials. Confidence is medium for exact terminology and design-intent judgements where external value-set expansions, ConceptMaps, official diffs, or Jira notes would improve the assessment.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Provenance keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 3 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 3 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 1 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 3, which creates meaningful stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 50/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Provenance.reason was removed and split/reframed as authorization plus why
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with `reason` uses a member not defined by the R6 base resource; there is also R6-to-R4 loss for `authorization` and `why`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Provenance.agent.onBehalfOf no longer permits Device or RelatedPerson and now represents delegation
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with `onBehalfOf` referencing Device or RelatedPerson can fail R6 target validation; retained targets also need semantic review because the field now means delegated authority.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Required Provenance.entity.role code set removed derivation and added instantiates/other
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the required R6 binding excludes an R4 code that was valid in the required R4 binding; generated enums and switch logic can also break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds local error constraints preventing self or circular delegation patterns on Provenance.agent
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance can fail R6 validation when `who` and `onBehalfOf` resolve to the same or equivalent party; runtime behavior depends on validator reference resolution.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Provenance.agent.role changed to structural-role semantics and a much narrower example value set
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: base validation still accepts old CodeableConcepts, but authorization, audit displays, picklists, and generated terminology helpers may interpret the same field differently.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 data may omit a timestamp required by R4; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism for this path.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using the new target types cannot be represented as base R4 without extension or policy, but there is no R4-to-R6 old-valid/new-invalid break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
